title: Cesure File v2
description: A .cesure tablature file, version 2: a JSON skeleton (metadata, tempo, repeats, tracks, measures with stable ids and time signatures, staves, voices) whose notes are written per voice in a compact text notation. Written by Cesure (https://cesure.app), meant to be read and written by agents and tools; the full specification is at https://cesure.app/format. Defaults are omitted on write. Every object keeps the keys it does not know, and the notation keeps the properties it does not know.

version.description: Format version. 2 for this schema; a reader refuses a higher one.

Score.description: The whole piece: metadata, the tempo, the repeats and the tracks.

album.description: Album, when the piece comes from one.

tempo.description: Initial tempo in quarter notes per minute, whatever the time signature (a 6/8 at 60 dotted quarters per minute is 90), in force until the first tempo change. Whole or not: 92.5 is kept as written.

tempoChanges.description: Tempo changes, each at the start of a measure named by its id. Empty = constant tempo.

repeats.description: Repeat signs, keyed by the id of the measure that carries them. A measure absent from this object carries none.

license.description: License of the published work (e.g. "Public Domain", "CC BY 4.0"). Empty = the file says nothing.

attribution.description: Attribution of the edition, including year and source URL when applicable. Travels with the file (CC-BY requires it). Empty = nothing to attribute.

tracks.description: The instrument tracks. Measure i of every track is the same column of the piece: same id, played at the same time.

TempoChange.description: A tempo taking effect at the start of a measure, until the next change.

measure.description: The id of the measure the tempo starts at. A change naming no measure of the piece is ignored.

tempo.description: Tempo in quarter notes per minute, whatever the time signature, from that measure on, whole or not.

Repeat.description: The repeat signs of one measure (of its column, on every track).

start.description: A repeated section opens at the start of this measure (|:).

end.description: A repeated section closes at the end of this measure (:|): the number of times the section is played in all. Absent = no close here.

endings.description: Alternative ending: the passes on which this measure is played ([1] = first ending, [2] = second). Absent or empty = played on every pass. A bracket longer than one measure repeats the passes on each of its measures.

tuning.description: Open string pitches from string 1 (the highest) to string N (the lowest); its length is the number of strings.

capo.description: Capo position in frets (0 = none). Tab numbers stay relative to the capo; only the sounding pitch shifts up.

volume.description: Track volume in the mix, 0..1. An arrangement property like `capo`: imported from Guitar Pro, saved and exported. Absent means 1 (full scale).

instrument.description: Timbre of the track, or null/absent = unspecified. Deliberately narrow: it lists only what a player can actually render. Absent is NOT "guitar" — it means the file says nothing, and a player should fall back to its own sound preference. May grow within v2: a reader treats a value it cannot name as unspecified, keeps it aside and writes it back unchanged.

measures.description: The measures of the track, in order.

Measure.description: One measure of a track: its id, its time signature and, per staff, its voices.

id.description: Stable id of the measure's column, the same on every track and never reused. Name ranges by it: it survives insertions and deletions, a measure number does not. Optional when writing a new measure: a reader assigns one.

numerator.description: Beats per measure (time signature numerator), 1 to 128. Not carried over: absent means 4, whatever the measure before. Cesure reads a value outside the range as 4.

denominator.description: Note value of one beat (time signature denominator). Not carried over: absent means 4, whatever the measure before.

staves.description: The staves of the track in this measure, top to bottom. Cesure writes one; a reader keeps the ones it cannot show and writes them back.

Staff.description: One staff of a track in one measure: its voices.

items.description: One voice of the staff in this measure, in the compact notation (https://cesure.app/format#the-compact-notation): beats separated by spaces; a beat is a note, a chord in parentheses, or r (rest), then .duration (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64), e.g. "5.3.4 (0.1 2.2).8 r.2". A note is fret.string, the string always written (x as fret: muted; {t} after the note: tied to the note it continues, its fret and string still written). Beat properties go in braces after the duration ({d} dotted, {dd} double-dotted, {tu 3} triplet, {tu (5 4)}), note properties in braces after the note ({h} hammer-on/pull-off, {sl} slide, {b (0 4)} bend in quarter tones, {v} vibrato, {lht} tap, {hand A|B}). Every beat states its duration after a dot; nothing carries over from the previous measure. A note may be written by its pitch instead (C4, F#3, Ebb4, Dx5): the reader chooses its string and fret. Reserved: a drum note by its General MIDI key (p42, p0 to p127). A property or note form a reader does not know is kept and written back.

voices.description: The voices of the staff, played at the same time, each over the whole measure and with its own rhythm: the first, then a second one (a bass under a melody) when there is one. Cesure writes at most two; a reader keeps the ones it cannot show and writes them back. Each voice should fill the time signature.

note.description: Pitch class. 's' suffix = sharp (e.g. Cs = C#). Closed for v1: a reader refuses a value it cannot name rather than guess the tuning, so adding one bumps the version.

octave.description: Octave number in scientific pitch notation. Middle C = {note: C, octave: 4}.
